extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalists, newsroom editors, and policy researchers interested in online news distribution and newsworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: Use measurable attention-concentration metrics to assess newsworthiness and how platform/search algorithms and legacy brands shape which stories reach mass audiences. Emphasizes operationalizing outlet attention share and the mechanisms that produce power-law concentration online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-Law Hyperlink Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A small number of political sites receive most links; the 'long tail' receives almost no links. The 'blogosphere' is dominated by a handful of bloggers; thousands of other blogs are essentially invisible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as an empirical metric of concentration: measure incoming link counts and the skew (e.g., power-law fit) to quantify how attention is distributed across sites; high skew indicates winner-take-all dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Engine Concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Most political queries direct users to the same top-ranked sites. Search engines amplify pre-existing concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via SERP analysis and click-through data for political queries; evaluate how search ranking funnels users to a narrow set of outlets and how ranking algorithms reinforce incumbent visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-20 Online News Concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite thousands of news sites, online news consumption concentrates on the top ~20 outlets — most of them legacy print/broadcast brands extending online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience-share metrics (traffic, unique visitors, time-on-site) to identify the small set of outlets that receive mass attention; consider top-n thresholds (e.g., top-20) when modeling national agenda-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainstream Blogger Demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Top political bloggers are disproportionately white, male, well-educated (~JD/PhD), and previously employed in elite institutions. The 'democratization' is restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include demographic and professional-background measures when evaluating representativeness of influential online voices; demographic skew signals limitations to claims of democratization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Concentration Greater Than Offline
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterintuitively, attention is more concentrated online than in print/broadcast — the opposite of early Internet predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare concentration measures across media (online vs. print/broadcast) to test claims about the Internet dispersing attention; higher online skew implies stronger selection effects online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferential Attachment (Rich-Get-Richer Linking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites with more incoming links receive more new links (rich-get-richer dynamic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model linking dynamics and network growth processes; preferential attachment predicts persistent dominance and should be accounted for when forecasting future concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Search Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Users prefer the small set of trusted sources rather than scanning many; they outsource discovery to search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat user cognitive costs as a behavioral constraint shaping consumption: measure click-depth, bounce rates, and reliance on familiar domains to understand selection patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm-Mediated Concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: PageRank and similar algorithms reward already-popular pages, accelerating concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how ranking/recommendation algorithms correlate with popularity and whether algorithmic design amplifies incumbents; consider algorithmic feedback loops when evaluating discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Time Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited attention forces sorting; users cluster on top sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In attention-weighted newsworthiness, account for finite user time (e.g., share of attention, time budgets) as a limiting factor that concentrates consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand Inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy outlets bring trust and habit from print/broadcast eras; born-digital outlets struggle to compete for attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brand/history variables (legacy status, offline reach) when evaluating an outlet's likely online attention share; legacy trust can be operationalized via historical circulation/ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach as a News Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Online, only stories on top-20 outlets reach mass audiences; selection by these outlets effectively determines national news agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operationalizing newsworthiness, weight stories by the outlet's reach/attention share rather than treating outlets equivalently; treat outlet reach as a primary determinant of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-Outlet Pseudo-Monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: A story on the New York Times homepage has orders of magnitude more attention than the same story on a smaller outlet — magnifies the selection power of major outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize outsized multiplicative effects of placement on major homepages; model placement effects separately from story quality when estimating likely audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-Visibility Premium (SEO as Tacit News Value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories optimized for search algorithms (titles, structured data, keyword density) reach more users; selection-for-SEO becomes a tacit news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate production practices (headline choice, metadata, schema, keyword use) as part of newsworthiness since they materially affect discoverability and audience size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Outlet Convergence (Pack Journalism Amplified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Top outlets converge on similar stories; concentrated online ecosystem amplifies pack journalism rather than dampening it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure story overlap among top outlets and the degree of agenda convergence; high overlap reduces diversity of issues reaching mass audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Tail Death (Niche Outlets Struggle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent / niche / alternative outlets struggle to reach scale; alternative news values get less traction than long-tail proponents predicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scalability prospects of niche outlets by examining referral patterns, linkage, and search visibility; lack of scale implies limited policy or agenda influence despite diversity of voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refutation of 'Anyone Can Be Heard' Assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Internet did not produce news-selection democratization; it produced a different kind of concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject naive assumptions of equal opportunity in online attention analyses; empirical concentration measures should be used to test claims of democratization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizability: Outlet Attention Share as Weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlet attention share is highly skewed and measurable; can be used as a weight in newsworthiness analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement attention-share weights (traffic, links, search referrals) in models of news impact and agenda-setting; provide concrete metrics rather than qualitative judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-Amplification Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm-mediated discovery (search, social feed, recommendations) concentrates rather than disperses attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include platform algorithm effects in any evaluation of news visibility; test for amplification by comparing pre- and post-algorithm exposure and routing.
